                        </ns0:gap>h</ns0:hi> the elder, by laying his Right-hand on his head, and his left on the others, and so a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dopts them to be his Children, gives them the Blessing of the Covenant, as to their Persons, and the Inheritance of two Tribes amongst his Sons, as belonging to <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> as his Birth-right, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 49.22, to 27. These by Faith he foretold, and applied particularly to each of them from God himself through Prayer.</ns0:note> Jacob when he was a dying, blessed both of the sons of Joseph, and <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Another Effect of his Faith, is his wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shipping God, having bequeathed his Body to the Burial in a firm Expectation of the promised Inheritance, as the Hi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />story clears, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 47.29, 30, 31. and 48.21, 22. For ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving sent for <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> he raiseth up himself on the Pillow at the Bed's head, and for his support used his <ns0:hi>Staff, leaning</ns0:hi> on the head of it, when in Faith he declares his Will to his Son <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> and binds him by an Oath to bury him in <ns0:hi>Mach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pelah</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> with <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Isaac,</ns0:hi> Heirs of the same Promise, as an Earnest and Handsel of the Twelve Tribes possessing it; which <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> having solemnly sworn to him, <ns0:hi>Iacob bowed</ns0:hi> himself and <ns0:hi>worshipped,</ns0:hi> lifting up his Heart to God in Thankfulness for his continual Providence in the gra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dual Accomplishment of his Promise to the Seed of <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob.</ns0:hi> This he <ns0:hi>did by Faith,</ns0:hi> adoring his Soveraign Lord and Saviour by his humbly bowing before him. There was no need of <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>bow</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Ioseph,</ns0:hi> who was inferior to <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> and blessed by him.</ns0:note> wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shipped, <ns0:hi>leaning</ns0:hi> upon the top of his staff.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:566" />22 By saith <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> the first Son of <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Rachel,</ns0:hi> whom God pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ferred before his Brethren, envied and sold by them, but advanced by him to be Lord of <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> and a Saviour to them, Heir of the Birth-right, and of his Father's Grace, a Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />triarch and Prophet like him, drawing near to the end of his Pilgrimage on Earth; and dying, <ns0:hi>he made mention,</ns0:hi> and brought to the mind of the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> his Children, Brethren, and Nephews; and, likely, with a charge to convey it down to their Posterity, as it might be remembred by them, that tho he did with willingness and choice, looking for a better Place and State than any in <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> and that his Death should not obstruct the Issues of Providence to them for good; for <ns0:hi>God lived,</ns0:hi> and would <ns0:hi>surely visit</ns0:hi> them in their Posterity, <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> living where he sent <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> to them, and would make them go up gloriously out of <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> and bring them into the Land of Promise, and give it to them for their Inheritance. This Testimony he gives them of it <ns0:hi>by Faith,</ns0:hi> Gen. 50.24. And God fulfilled it 160 years after his Death, as he had sworn to <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Joseph when he died, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>remembred.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> made mention of the departing of the children of Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rael: And <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>By Faith</ns0:hi> likewise he charged them about carrying his <ns0:hi>imbalmed Body</ns0:hi> with them, and burying it in <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> and obliged the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> to it by an Oath, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 50.25. making it an Earnest and Signal to them of the Promise and Oath of God for their Deliverance, that as he desired his <ns0:hi>Bones</ns0:hi> might be buried in <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> being Heir together with <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> of the same promised Inheritance, it might be a visible token of, and Incouragement, in the ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pointed time, to their Return. And this <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> fulfilled, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 13.19. carrying them away with them, and afterwards bu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rying of them in <ns0:hi>Shechem,</ns0:hi> the Lot of <ns0:hi>Ephraim, Iosh.</ns0:hi> 24.32.</ns0:note> gave commandment concerning his bones.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 By faith <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The Parents of <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> were as eminent <ns0:hi>in this Faith</ns0:hi> as their Progenitors; for by it <ns0:hi>Amram</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iochebed</ns0:hi> both of them of the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Levi,</ns0:hi> Exod. 6.20. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> here put by a Metaphrase for <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, and tho in the History ascribed to the Mother only, yet it was by the Father's direction, as <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 2.2. comp. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 7.20. <ns0:hi>They hid Moses born,</ns0:hi> under the bloody Edict of a Tyrant for drowning all the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi>-males in <ns0:hi>Nile</ns0:hi>: he was born three years after <ns0:hi>Aaron,</ns0:hi> and 65 after <ns0:hi>Io<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />seph</ns0:hi>'s Death, they kept three Months from the Destroyers, and they adventured the Penalties threatned by the Edict, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 2.2, 3. Faith overcoming their Fears and Difficulties about it, and in all Probability, ordered their fitting the Ark, and dispose of it for his Preservation with the other Acts attending it.</ns0:note> Moses when he was born was hid three months of his parents, because they <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The Reason of Faith's Work, was their seeing of him to be <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>fair,</ns0:hi> beautiful, proper; and this not in himself only, but as <ns0:hi>Stephen</ns0:hi> interpre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s it, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 7.20. <ns0:hi>Fair to God.</ns0:hi> Some glorious Aspect was by God put upon him as a Signal of some great Person, and of great use in God's Design to his Church; some extraordinary Stamp of God on his Countenance, which Faith could discern there, and so influence them to conceal and preserve him.</ns0:note> saw <ns0:hi>he was</ns0:hi> a proper child, and they were <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> made them <ns0:hi>fearless</ns0:hi>; for they were not afraid that the King's Edict should frustrate Gods Purpose concerning the Child, or keep him from its Service to the Church, where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in God would imploy him, and of which he had given them a Signal in that lustre cast on his Person, and therefore they used means to preserve him, even when they exposed him, and which had a suitable success, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 2.3, to 10.</ns0:note> not afraid of the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 1.16, 22.</ns0:note> kings commandment.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 By faith <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> himself was as eminent a <ns0:hi>Believer</ns0:hi> as his Parents, and a mighty Instance of <ns0:hi>Divine Faith.</ns0:hi> He who was so named and saved by the Enemies of the Church, and adopted as a Son to a notorious one of them, yet being <ns0:hi>great in Age and Stature</ns0:hi> full forty, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 3.11. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 7.23. past the folly of Childhood and rashness of Youth, upon manly Delibe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ration and a rational Exercise of Faith, notwithstanding he was by Birth a poor <ns0:hi>Israelite,</ns0:hi> and saved from perishing by a Princess, the Daughter of a Potent King: nourished through her Indulgence by his own Mother, adopted as her own Son, educated by her in all the Wisdom of the <ns0:hi>Egyptians,</ns0:hi> preferred, owned, and honoured as her Son; and might have been in a fair way to have succeeded to the Kingdom; yet not out of any Disingenuity, or base Ingratitude to his eminent Preserver, but out of a <ns0:hi>Divine Faith</ns0:hi> he layeth down all his Titles and Honours, and renounceth his Relation, for the Enjoyment of a better Title with, and a greater Good in God; and this he manifested by Word and Deed in his after Transactions, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 25.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 2.10, 11.</ns0:note> Moses when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaohs daughter,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 84.10.</ns0:note> Chusing <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The same Faith influenced his Will, the Cause of his <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ormer Renunciation, for being in the present Fruition of all Court-favours, and under the Offers of all worldly Delights by <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> and of all worldly Discontents by God: <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> determined his Choice, made him a <ns0:hi>Fellow-Sufferer</ns0:hi> in all the Oppressions, Afflictions, Persecutions of his natural Brethren the People of God, the most priviledged Society in the World for hope, as the most exercised by Tryals for God's sake; he knew there would be eternal Rest and Glory into which they would issue him, beside glorious Effects they would have on his Soul while he was enduring them; and that they were but passing, and would quickly have an end, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.18. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4.17, 18.</ns0:note> rather to suffer afflictions with the people of God, than <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The same <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> made him to re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ject the enticing Pleasures of Sin, which could not be avoided by his continuance in <ns0:hi>Pharaoh</ns0:hi>'s Court, either in dissembling himself to be no <ns0:hi>Israelite,</ns0:hi> professing himself to be an <ns0:hi>Egyp<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tian,</ns0:hi> taking part with them in their cruel Carriage to his Brethren, living after their vicious Course in all manner of Voluptuousness, and the Pleasures which he was to enjoy were sinful, transitory and momentaneous, neither satisfying, nor enduring, and must be attended with a Sting in the end of them, even eternal Anguish and Torment, whereas his Afflictions would end in eternal Joys and Pleasures. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 9.43, 44, 47. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 16.25.</ns0:note> to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 Esteeming <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> influenced and determined his former Choice from the most excellent Ground of it, the Representation of these by the divine inspired Truth to him: It made him weigh and deliberate about the matters proposed, and then to judge, and positively determine about them, That the re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />proachful Suffering of all sorts of Afflictions, Poverty, Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stresses, Tortures most ignominiously inflicted on them by their Enemies for their Faith in Christ, and Expectation of him according to God's Promise, and who was now the An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gel of the Covenant that protected them, as well as their Ancestor <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> Gen. 48.15, 16. These <ns0:hi>Moses chose,</ns0:hi> to suffer patiently out of Faith in, and Love to Christ: these, with what excellent things were to follow by virtue of God's Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mise, he preferred as a better and richer Estate, and infinitely more desireable than all the <ns0:hi>Treasures</ns0:hi> of Honours and Riches, which either <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> or its King could oblige him with, the whole of them founded in the Dust, disposed by Flesh, fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding in Enjoyment, and ending in Vanity. What, are these Treasures, compared to those laid up in store by Christ for his in Heaven?</ns0:note> the reproach <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>for Christ.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> of Christ grea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter riches then the treasures in Egypt: For he <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">These were the things <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> had in his Eye, <ns0:hi>the end</ns0:hi> of Christ's Reproach, and <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi>'s Glory; this made him turn his Eye and Heart away from <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> and intently to look on the excellent Issue of his reproachful Sufferings for Christ, even <ns0:hi>Christ rendring</ns0:hi> to him his unexpressibly glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rious and eternal <ns0:hi>Reward</ns0:hi> for it, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4.17, 18. This God had promised to, Christ had purchased for such, who were by Faith bearing his Reproach, and qualified for the enjoy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of it. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.17, 18. 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.12. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 4.13, 14.</ns0:note> had respect unto the recompence of the re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 By faith <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 13.17, 18.</ns0:note> he <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">By the same excellent <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> after his demand from <ns0:hi>Pha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />raoh</ns0:hi> of Liberty for <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> to leave <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> and had brought on him and his People the Ten Plagues God threatned them with, then he brake the Bands of Captivity, and took up <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> and le<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> subdued, wasted by Plagues, and a place to be abhorred, triumphing over it, he forsakes it as a Conqueror, and carrieth away the Spoils of it. The <ns0:hi>Wrath</ns0:hi> and Rage of <ns0:hi>Pharaoh</ns0:hi> at him and his Work for <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> did not apale him; he was not afraid of his threatning to kill him, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 10.28, 29. yet he defied him, even when his Rage made him to pursue him and <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> with his host, to destroy them.</ns0:note> forsook Egypt, not fear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the wrath of the king: For he <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>he was of a bold undaunted Spirit,</ns0:hi> so as nothing was too hard for him, either to suffer or do: Magnanimity expelled his Fear, so as he would stand or march according to God's order, Faith presenting to his View at all times the great Angel of the Covenant, God the Son, the Redeemer of him and <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> the only Potentate, <ns0:hi>the invisible King of Kings,</ns0:hi> and Lord of Lords, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 6.14, 15, 16. with him, and for him against <ns0:hi>Pharaoh,</ns0:hi> leading, covering, and guarding him and <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> in all the way, and fulfilling his Promise of deli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vering of his Church from <ns0:hi>Egppt</ns0:hi>; this makes him to march undauntedly with God's Host.</ns0:note> endured as seeing him who is invisible.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 Through faith <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">This <ns0:hi>Divine Faith</ns0:hi> influenced him in all his Work about God's Ordinances, receiving the Law about him, from God's Mouth, and obeying it: By it he <ns0:hi>made</ns0:hi> the Passover, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> as God's Instrument, he instituted it, and put it into being, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.21. he celebrated & solemnly managed in each particular, and finished it, reaching the end of it according to God's Law in that behalf, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5.7. Here he saw Christ, and testified of him, the true <ns0:hi>Paschal Lamb</ns0:hi> of God; by whom God's Wrath passed over the Children of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> when it rested upon the <ns0:hi>Egyptians, Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.21. &c. <ns0:hi>By Faith</ns0:hi> he took a <ns0:hi>bunch of Hysop</ns0:hi> and dipt it in <ns0:hi>the Blood of the Paschal Lamb,</ns0:hi> and striked the Lintel and two Side-posts of the Doors with the Blood, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.22. He used it as a Signal of God's sparing <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> and passing over their Houses by his Angel, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 23. and he saw in it the <ns0:hi>true Blood of sprinkling,</ns0:hi> of Christ our Passover, which saveth Souls from the Destroyer, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 5.46. and brings them out of the <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> of this World into the heavenly <ns0:hi>Canaan.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The end of both these, was, That the destroying Angel, who slew all the First-born of the <ns0:hi>Egyptians,</ns0:hi> might not touch an <ns0:hi>Israelite,</ns0:hi> Exod. 12.29, 30. Under all this <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> evidenced to <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> God's Faithfulness in his Promise, it order<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed all his Duty, and it realized to their hope in that time of Danger, that God would save them, who were under <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>hat Blood, working their Assurance of it.</ns0:note> that destroy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed the first-born, should touch them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:566" />29 By faith <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The same <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> enabled <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> eminently, and those o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther Believers, as <ns0:hi>Aaron, Caleb, Ioshua,</ns0:hi> &c. for all <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved not, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.5. yet for the Faithful's sake were they kept from drowning, after <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> had, at God's command, (when the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> were ready to be fallen on by the <ns0:hi>E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gyptians</ns0:hi>) lifted up his Rod, and stretched his Hand over the Red-Sea, when God immediately, by an East-wind, divided it, made the Waters to stand up on each side like Walls of Chrystal, and the bottom of it to be dry; then entred <ns0:hi>Mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> into the empty and dry space, and <ns0:hi>walked</ns0:hi> through it <ns0:hi>on dry Ground,</ns0:hi> and not a Soul of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> miscarryed, but might see astonishing Power and Mercy in it; <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> ch. 14.22.</ns0:note> they passed through the red-sea, as by dry <ns0:hi>land</ns0:hi>: which the Egyptians assay<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">In the mean time the <ns0:hi>Egyptians, with their King,</ns0:hi> pursuing <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> for their Ruine, find their own, for presum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ptuously adventuring to pursue them through this miracu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lous space, guided by Sense, and not by Faith, and thinking to pass as safe as <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> when they had <ns0:hi>no Word</ns0:hi> for it, God troubles them by his Angels in their mot<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>on, makes them drive heavily; and having brought them into his Pit in the midst of the Channel, the Chrystal-Walls dissolve, and the Waters returning to their fluid Nature, quickly overwhelm'd and swallowed up all that Host, so as not one of these unbe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieving, presumptuous, persecuting Wretches escaped. God's great Work in this, as to <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> had a double meaning; <ns0:hi>literal,</ns0:hi> their <ns0:hi>Salvation from the</ns0:hi> Egyptians; <ns0:hi>mystical,</ns0:hi> their <ns0:hi>baptismal Initiation into the Covenant of God</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>; tho all of them had not Faith unfeigned, yet professed Faith in God; and the Doctrine <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> brought from him, was accounted sufficient to attain both, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.2.</ns0:note> to do, were drowned.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 By faith <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">This <ns0:hi>Divine Faith</ns0:hi> exercised by <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> after their entrance into the Land of Promise (who did, on God's Word and Command, compass the impregnable Walls of <ns0:hi>Iericho</ns0:hi> once every day for six days together, and on the seventh day seven times, sounding with Trumpets of Rams-Horns, and at last giving a shout) brought down these Walls flat to the Ground by the Almighty Power of God, to whom they were as nothing, <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> ch. 6.20. Faith in all this realized God's Promise to them, reached forth their love to him, and Obedience in all Particulars required by him, glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rifying God, as the great Captain of their Hosts, as he re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vealed himself, <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> 5.13, 14, 15. committing the Work and Event to him, who, by the Breath of Faith, doth crum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble down these Walls before them.</ns0:note> the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were compassed about seven days.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 By faith the harlot <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">By the same <ns0:hi>Gospel-Faith Rahab,</ns0:hi> who, as the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> read the word, <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> 2.1. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap> was an <ns0:hi>Hostess,</ns0:hi> and kept an House of Entertainment, and so came to lodge the Spies: Or, as the <ns0:hi>Septuagint</ns0:hi> read it, and the Holy Ghost confirms it here, and <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 2.25. was <ns0:hi>a publick Harlot,</ns0:hi> who gat her Liveli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hood by the Prostitution of her Body, as well as the Sale of Meat and Drink; so notorious a Sinner as she, and a <ns0:hi>Canaanite</ns0:hi> too, was preserved from the Destruction that was inflicted by the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> on the unbelieving and disobedient Inhabitants of <ns0:hi>Iericho,</ns0:hi> being, after her Exclusion out of the Camp, in order to a legal Purifying, admitted into God's Church, and honoured by him to be a Mother in <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> from whom the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> should descend, <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> 6.23, 25.</ns0:note> Rahab perished not with them <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>that were disob<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>dient.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> that believed not, when <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">The full Proof of her being a Believer, was her entertaining of the Spies sent from <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Iericho,</ns0:hi> preserving them when sought for, and dismissing them, advising them what they were to do in order to their safety, <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> 2.3, 10, to the end. The ground of all this, was her <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> in God's Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mise of giving <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> confirmed by the great Works she heard God had done for them, and her own Expectation of Good only in the Portion of God's People, to whom she desired to be united, which was afterwards accomplished. Neither doth <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> contradict each other concerning her Faith and Works, <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 2.25. For she was exempted from Destruction by the same Faith by which she was justified; and her Faith was justified to be sound and true, by her carriage to the Spies, for it was a full Demonstration of her Faith in God.</ns0:note> she had re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceived the spies with peace.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 And <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Here the Spirit puts a Period to the <ns0:hi>Induction,</ns0:hi> by an Expostulation, as if he had said, Why do I speak of so many Examples of Faith? <ns0:hi>the Old Testament is full of them</ns0:hi>; but here's Proof enough, Il'e say no more.</ns0:note> what shall I more say? for <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For time of Li<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e and Writing</ns0:hi> would be sooner gone, than a full Account can be given of all the notable Effects of Faith by all these Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thies who might be named; yet he would give some gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral hints of Persons, and of the Works of Faith, which he judgeth sufficient, and so nameth promiscuously, and not in order of time wherein they existed. He <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ameth four Judges, one King, and one Prophet, and extraordinary Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets in a bulk, whose Histories you have, of <ns0:hi>Gideon,</ns0:hi> Judg. <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 6.11. &c. <ns0:hi>Barak,</ns0:hi> Judg, 4.5. &c. <ns0:hi>Samson,</ns0:hi> Judg. 13.14.15.16. <ns0:hi>Iephtha,</ns0:hi> Judg. 11.12. <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s History and <ns0:hi>Samuel</ns0:hi>'s in the first and second Books of <ns0:hi>Samuel,</ns0:hi> and the first of <ns0:hi>Chronicles.</ns0:hi> The excellent Exploits of whose Faith, are, as their Names, enumerated promiscuously; some of them agreeing to par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ticular Persons, others to them all.</ns0:note> the time would fail me to tell of Gideon, and <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> Barak, and <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> Samson, and <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> Jephtha, and <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Sam. 16.13.</ns0:note> David also, and Samuel, and <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 Who through faith <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">These, by the same <ns0:hi>Gospel-Faith, subdued Kingdoms,</ns0:hi> de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />feating the mighty Enemies of the Church; and eminently amongst them, <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> who conquered <ns0:hi>Edom, Moab, Ammon,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Syrian</ns0:hi> Kingdoms, and extended his Conques<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s to <ns0:hi>Euphrates.</ns0:hi> This he and they did in obedience to God's Call, in dependance on God's Promise both of Conduct and Victory. All was done by God's Arm at the Instance of Faith and Prayer, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 18.29, to 42. and 20.5, 9.</ns0:note> subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">They were all of them eminently righteous in their Persons, and in their <ns0:hi>Administration of Iustice</ns0:hi> to others; the utmost of their Abilities were laid out in it, as became righteous Judges as to all matters of God and Men, <ns0:hi>Iudg. ch.</ns0:hi> 6. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 7.15, 17. and 12.2, 6.</ns0:note>, obtained <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">A <ns0:hi>real and actual Possession of all those good Things, which God secured to them by Promise,</ns0:hi> especially as to <ns0:hi>Gideon</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Barack,</ns0:hi> Victory and Success over the <ns0:hi>Canaanites</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Midianites, Iudg. ch.</ns0:hi> 4, and 6. <ns0:hi>Samson</ns0:hi> Victory over the <ns0:hi>Philistines; David</ns0:hi> Victory over the Churches Enemies. All which they first obtained in the Promise, and then in the Execution. <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> secured all, giving a real Enjoyment of all the Good made theirs in the Promise, and then in the Event; and will give the fulness of all Good in general Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mises made to the Church and them in the end.</ns0:note> promises, stopped <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> an eminent Prophet of God believed in him, and for his Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stimony to him, was cast into the Den of Lions to be de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />voured, where <ns0:hi>God stops the Mouths</ns0:hi> of them on his <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Prayer,</ns0:hi> and opens them to destroy their Adversaries, <ns0:hi>Dan. ch.</ns0:hi> 6.22. By the Power and Strength of God, both <ns0:hi>Samson</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> slew those Lyons which would have preyed both on them and others, <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 14.6. and 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 17.34, 35, 36. Faith obtained this Success for them.</ns0:note> the mouths of lyons,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Quenched <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">By the same Faith others of the <ns0:hi>Prophets, v.</ns0:hi> 32. emi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nently acquainted with God, and Partakers of his <ns0:hi>Secret,</ns0:hi> who defying Idolatry, and the Threatnings of a Tyrant, became Confessors of the true God and his Worship, and were ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />judged to the fiery Furnace, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 3.19, 23. and by Faith were secured from being consumed by those Flames, and which in an Instant destroyed those which threw them in, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 22, to 28. How did this fetch down the Son of God himself to accompany them, and to suspend the consuming Power of the Fire, so as it did not <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>inge either their Persons or Garments, or to leave any Scent of it upon them? And how did <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s Prayers extinguish the Fire at <ns0:hi>Ki<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />broth-hattaavah,</ns0:hi> and at <ns0:hi>Tabberah,</ns0:hi> Num. 11.1, 3. and 16.22, to 46.</ns0:note> the violence of fire, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Sam. 20.1. 1 King. 19.3. 2 King. 6.16.</ns0:note> escaped <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">By Faith these Worthies fore-mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 32. were delivered, when others fell by the devouring Sword, and all those Instruments of War which were destructive to others. Their Enemies fell by their Swords in those many Battels wherein they were engaged, fulfilling at that time God's Will, and trusting on his Promise. And how many of the Prophets hath God delivered from the Swords of those who would have killed them?</ns0:note> the edge of the sword, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">2 King. 20.7. Job 42.10.</ns0:note> out of weakness <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">By Faith many of those who had many natural <ns0:hi>Infirmities,</ns0:hi> both of <ns0:hi>Body</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mind,</ns0:hi> had their Tremblings and Faintings of Spirit, and were, in re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spect of their Enemies, weak, few in number, short of them, as to Force, Power and Policy, yet by Faith in God, were made bold as <ns0:hi>Lions,</ns0:hi> and had wonderful Success against numerous and potent Enemies, <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 4.8. and 6.15, 16. and 7.5, 7, 10, and 11.29. and 15.15, 11, 19. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 7.9, 10. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> were made strong, waxed valiant in fight <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Faith made those who were called to the War by God, mighty for that Service, 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 22.30, to 38. so as no Perils could daunt them, no Service was too hard for them. How victorious in the most desperate At<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tempts, as to sense, did Faith make them? <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 27.1, 3.</ns0:note>, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.<ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">They overthrew the Camps of Adversaries. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap>
notes a single <ns0:hi>Castle</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Tower,</ns0:hi> Acts 21.34. or a whole Camp or Place where an Army is pitched, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 13.11, 13. in the plural, many such <ns0:hi>Tents</ns0:hi> where Soldiers lie; and is me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tonymically read <ns0:hi>Armies.</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> actively taken, is <ns0:hi>to make to lie down,</ns0:hi> or to <ns0:hi>throw</ns0:hi> down, as applied to Tents and <ns0:hi>Camps,</ns0:hi> to put to <ns0:hi>flight,</ns0:hi> as applied to <ns0:hi>Armies</ns0:hi>; all which were those of the idolatrous Enemies of the Church, <ns0:hi>Stran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gers</ns0:hi> to their Country, and more to their God, as the Army and Camp of <ns0:hi>Midian,</ns0:hi> Judg. 7.13, to 23. which were over<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />turned, routed, and destroyed by them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:567" />35 Women <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Through this <ns0:hi>Divine Faith,</ns0:hi> both the Prophets <ns0:hi>Elijah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Elisha,</ns0:hi> did raise and restore, the one to the Widow of <ns0:hi>Serepta,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 17.22, 23. the other to the <ns0:hi>Shunamite,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 4.35, 36, their Sons from the dead; and these Women and Mothers did by <ns0:hi>Faith receive them from</ns0:hi> the Prophets alive again, who by Faith and Prayer procured this Mercy from the quickning Lord, for them. In the general Resurrection all shall be raised by the Power of God, and the effect of Faith therein is only receptive; we shall enjoy Life again, and re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive others from the dead also.</ns0:note> received their dead raised to life again: and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 22.25.</ns0:note> others <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Others</ns0:hi> also, besides the Prophets fore-mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 32. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, were <ns0:hi>tym<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />panised</ns0:hi>; what manner of torturing Death this was, is not so certain, whether by <ns0:hi>Excoriation,</ns0:hi> and making <ns0:hi>Drum-heads</ns0:hi> of their Skins, or extending them on the Rack, as the Skin or Parchment is on the Drum-head, and then with Clubs, or other Instruments, beating them to Death; of which sort of Sufferers seems <ns0:hi>Eleazer</ns0:hi> to be under <ns0:hi>Antiochus Epiphanes,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Mac.</ns0:hi> 6.19, 30. for his not turning Heathen, when urged to it by that Torture; and tho his <ns0:hi>Deliverance</ns0:hi> from Tor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture and Death were offered to him by his Tormentors on his Compliance with them, and renouncing his Religion, yet he refu<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ed it as others did, 2 <ns0:hi>Mac.</ns0:hi> 7.24. resolving to endure the utmost Extremity cather than turn Idolater, and disobey God.</ns0:note> were tortured, not accepting deliverance, that <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">That which influenced them to suffer, was their Faith in God's Promise of obtaining thereby a Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection to an incomparable better Life than they could have enjoyed on Earth; for tho they might have been spared from Death now threatned them, which was <ns0:hi>a kind of Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />surrection,</ns0:hi> yet was it not to be compared with the Resurrection to eternal Life, Glory, Bliss, and Pleasure, to be injoyed by them with God in Heaven; see what influenced them, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 17, 18.</ns0:note> they might obtain a better resurrection.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And others <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The same Gospel-Faith inabled others, than those men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned before, Prophets and Saints, as <ns0:hi>Micaiah,</ns0:hi> 1 King. 22.24. <ns0:hi>Elishah,</ns0:hi> 2 King. 2.23. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 8.18. <ns0:hi>Amos ch.</ns0:hi> 7.10. readily, chearfully, and patiently to accept and receive the Expe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rience and Trials of <ns0:hi>mocking,</ns0:hi> from the insulting, cruel Ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies of God and his Church, both national and Aliens, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing exposed and made a Laughing-stock by Reproaches, Sar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />casms, and Nick-names, to aggravate their Afflictions, and these inflicted on them by Words and external Signs, Tri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />als, which to an ingenuous Spirit bears harder than external Torments, and which they more deeply sense and resent; yet <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> makes them to receive all humbly, and carrieth them above them, as <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 31.20. and 52.1, to 5. and 120.3, 4. and 140.3.</ns0:note> had trial of <ns0:hi>cruel</ns0:hi> mockings and <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">They felt the <ns0:hi>Scourges</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Whips</ns0:hi> of their Enemies <ns0:hi>Smart</ns0:hi> on them, such as were excessively shame<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful and painful, being inflicted on the vilest Persons, as <ns0:hi>Slaves</ns0:hi>; such as was the matter of these Scourges, such their Smart<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ings, whether of Thongs, Cords, or Wires, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 20.2. and 37.15. This Torment was commonly inflicted on them, not in <ns0:hi>Antiochus</ns0:hi>'s time only, and those before, but commonly in Christ's and the Apostles days, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 6.5. and 11.23.</ns0:note> scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">They chearfully and patiently submitted to the cruel treating of their Persecutors, who <ns0:hi>put them in the Stocks,</ns0:hi> places of little <ns0:hi>Ease, Dungeons,</ns0:hi> loading them with Iron <ns0:hi>Shackels</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Fetters,</ns0:hi> which the Wickeness of Man had invented to torment them with; stern and cruel usage by their Goalers, restraining So<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciety from them, and of comfortable Relief, feeding them with the Bread and Water of Affliction, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 18.26. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 16.24.</ns0:note>, and imprisonment.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 King. 21.13.</ns0:note> They <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">By the same <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> were several of the Prophets and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieving Worthies of old carried through <ns0:hi>cruel Deaths,</ns0:hi> the just Punishment of Malefactors, but the wicked Tortures of these innocent Saints, some being stoned to Death, as <ns0:hi>Zacharias</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Iehoiada,</ns0:hi> 2 Chron. 24.21. And others, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 21.35. and 23.37. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 13.34.</ns0:note> were stoned, they were <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">As <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> was, is a known Tra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dition among the <ns0:hi>Hebrews,</ns0:hi> a Punishment common among the bordering Nations of them, 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 12.31. <ns0:hi>Amos</ns0:hi> 1.3. and exercised on these Innocents, to which Christ himself alludeth <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 24.51.</ns0:note> sawn asunder, were <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Whether <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> should not be <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, is much doubted, <ns0:hi>Temptation</ns0:hi> being no manner of <ns0:hi>Death</ns0:hi>; and the Spirit had instanced in it before, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 35. It may therefore be a slip of the Transcriber, and that <ns0:hi>Burning</ns0:hi> was the cruel Death that should fill this place among the rest, a common Punishment with them, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 29.22. 2 <ns0:hi>Maccab.</ns0:hi> 7.5. Or, it may note a <ns0:hi>Death</ns0:hi> with several Trials of Racks and Torments gradually inflicted, with a Design <ns0:hi>to tempt them</ns0:hi> by their Pains to renounce their Religion.</ns0:note> tempted, were slain <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Others were killed by the Sword, either by <ns0:hi>beheading,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>cutting in pieces,</ns0:hi> Mark 6.16, 17. A kind of Death foretold to be attending the Mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tyrs of Jesus Christ, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 20.4. All these sorts of Death were most unjustly and cruelly inflicted on them by their Persecutors, and as patiently received, and chearfully under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gone by them.</ns0:note> with the sword, they <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">As Faith carried these Believers through variety of Deaths, so it managed others comfortably under their <ns0:hi>Banishments</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>lingring Sufferings,</ns0:hi> which were in propor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion as cruel as Death it self; they circuited up and down to preserve themselves from their Destroyers, either volun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tarily returning themselves into desolate places to keep a good Conscience, or were unjustly and violently banished and forced away from their own Habitations, to live as Vagabonds, cloathed only with Goat-skins and Sheep-skins, the common Apparel of the Prophets, as of <ns0:hi>Elijah,</ns0:hi> 2 King. 1.8. <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 13.4. which they wore as they came from the Beasts back, without dressing,</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Matth. 3.4.</ns0:note> wandred about in sheep-skins, and goat-skins, being destitute <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Wandring in this forlorn state, <ns0:hi>stript of</ns0:hi> Money, and Necessaries of Life, and not sup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plied by others in their Poverty, 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 17.4. grievously pressed within, pained without, and afflicted beyond what can be sensed by any, but in the like States, and evilly intreat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed by all; many Miseries attending them by their Pursuers, Hardship in Travels, and all sorts of Evils, which multiplied their Griess: Through all this Faith carried them comfor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tably, and kept God with them.</ns0:note>, afflicted, tor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mented:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 Of whom <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">The Spirit intermixeth an Account of what these Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons were, who were so treated, lest the Reader or Hearer of these things might be mistaken of them, judging them to be some <ns0:hi>heinous Malefactors,</ns0:hi> who were thus hurried in, and destroyed by the World. VVould you know what manner of Persons they were; be it known to you in the Judgment of God, the best Judge of their Persons and States; they were such as <ns0:hi>the World did not deserve they should live among them,</ns0:hi> but were unworthy of their Society, and the Blessings which did attend it; and were it not for their sakes, God would quickly put an End to the sinful World, and burn it up. Such were these as did more for the Preservation of the VVorld, when thus brutishly treated by it, than it would or could do for it self.</ns0:note> the world was not worthy they wandred in <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Yet were they wandring over the desolate Parts of this Earth, being forced from all Society with Men, to the retirements of wild Beasts in Deserts, and climbing up Mountains and Rocks from their Persecutors, lodg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing themselves in the natural or artificial Dens and Caves of the Earth, the only Receptacles for these VVorthies, Faith giving them the best Company, God and his Comforts there; See 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 22.23, 24. 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 17.3. and 18.13. 1 <ns0:hi>Mac.</ns0:hi> 1.53. and 2.28.29, 30.</ns0:note> deserts, and <ns0:hi>in</ns0:hi> mountains, and <ns0:hi>in</ns0:hi> dens and caves of the earth.</ns0:p>

                     </ns0:gap> strictly is <ns0:hi>having been martyred,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>made Mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tyrs,</ns0:hi> specially <ns0:hi>witnessing</ns0:hi> to the Death for Christ, have a <ns0:hi>Testi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mony</ns0:hi> given to them, by way of Eminency, by <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi> himself in his Scripture-Record, that through Faith they pleased him in their glorious Atchievements and Sufferings, and were God's faithful VVitnesses to the VVorld, glorifying him in it, tho reproached and ruined by the VVorld, yet they were too good to live in it, and were fit to live with him in Heaven, as <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 2, 5, 16, 35.</ns0:note> a good report through faith, received not the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mise <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Yet these VVorthies, as <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> and his believing Seed, did not possess the Land of <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> tho they had the Promise of it in their time, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 13. others did obtain the Grace and good things promised for their time, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 33. but none of these had fulfilled to them in their day the Manifestation of the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> in the Flesh; tho they saw his Day and Coming by Faith, and did rejoice in it, yet none saw him so come as <ns0:hi>Simeon</ns0:hi> did, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 2.26, 29. tho as to the eternal Benefits by Christ they did as actually re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive them, as those since his perfecting the Work of Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />demption have received them, even eternal Blessedness and Glory by him, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 15.11.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:567" />40 God <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The causes of their not receiving the Promise, are summed up in this Verse; the efficient of it is God's Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vidence unto Believers before and after the incarnation of the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>; God having from Eternity <ns0:hi>foreknowledg</ns0:hi> of those who would believe in God the Son incarnate, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.29. predestinated them to be called to the Faith in Him, and <ns0:hi>provided better</ns0:hi> for New-Testament-Believers than for the Old ones, that what they had of Christ in <ns0:hi>Types and Vails,</ns0:hi> these should have in <ns0:hi>Truth</ns0:hi>; what these had in <ns0:hi>Promise,</ns0:hi> they should have in <ns0:hi>Sight</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Possession</ns0:hi>; what these had in <ns0:hi>Hope,</ns0:hi> as to his first coming, they should have it <ns0:hi>past,</ns0:hi> and it as an earnest of his second Coming; what they had by <ns0:hi>mea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sure</ns0:hi> of his Spirit and Grace, these should have in <ns0:hi>fulness. Luke</ns0:hi> 10.23, 24. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.14, 16. and 7.39. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 3.8. <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 3.8, 9, 10, 11. <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> 2.13. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.12.</ns0:note> having <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>foreseen.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> provided some better thing for us, that they <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The final cause of this Gracious Providence was, that the former and later Believers might be <ns0:hi>compleated together,</ns0:hi> they shall not reach that perfect state of Grace and Glory by a reunion of their Bodies and Souls until the general Resurrection, when they shall not prevent us, nor we them; but as soon as the Trumpet alarms the Dead to rise, in the same mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, and twinkling of an Eye shall the Living be changed, and all be caught up together in the Clouds, to meet the Lord in the Air, and so shall be ever with the Lord, 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 4.15, to 18. The ground of which Perfection of all Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lievers in all Ages being in the last time, is from his choosing them all to be but one body of Christ, and him their Head; so as one Member cannot be perfected but in the perfection of the whole, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 8.11. <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 4.4. In which perfection of it, God is resolved to be all in all; not in one, or in some, but when Christ hath sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dued all his Enemies, and gathered all his Members, then shall his Body and Kingdom be perfected, and God be all in all, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.28.</ns0:note> without us should not be made perfect <ns0:hi>g.</ns0:hi>
